answer: Staggered arrival windows. The system grants each verified identity a velvet slot in a slowly releasing queue, so fresh agents must wait out a minimum inter-arrival gap before acting. Mass-registered sybils bunch into one narrow burst and get flagged like a spiral of duplicate timestamps, since real demand spreads across hours. A farmer therefore pays wall-clock delay per identity and needs a separate isolated island of accounts, each aged independently, making duplication costly in time rather than tokens.
